llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed dLazy image-generation CLI wrapper, with expected external API use and credential storage for that purpose.

dimensions.detail: Network access to api.dlazy.com and files.dlazy.com, prompt submission, and upload of user-specified media files are disclosed and proportionate for cloud image generation.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The skill declares npm/npx installation of the pinned @dlazy/cli version 1.2.2 and provides provenance links; this is normal for a CLI-backed SaaS skill but still depends on a third-party npm package.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The trigger keywords include generic image-generation phrases, which could activate the skill more broadly than a provider-specific trigger, but the runtime instructions themselves are limited to using the dLazy banana2 command and handling auth or balance errors.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The skill documents that login or auth set stores an API key in ~/.dlazy/config.json, with per-invocation DLAZY_API_KEY as an alternative; this persistence is disclosed and revocable.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The stated purpose is generating and editing images with Nano Banana 2.0, and the documented command, parameters, uploads, and hosted output URLs all align with that purpose.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Before installing, confirm you want dLazy/Nano Banana 2.0 to handle the prompts and any image paths you provide. Prefer npx or review the pinned npm package if you do not want a global CLI install, and use the per-run DLAZY_API_KEY option if you do not want the API key saved in the CLI config.
llm.findings:
[SQP-1] expected: The English artifact uses broad image-generation trigger phrases alongside Nano Banana-specific triggers; this is a scoping note, not evidence of hidden behavior, because the SaaS data flow and authentication requirements are disclosed.
[SQP-1] expected: The Chinese artifact mirrors the same broad trigger phrasing; it could cause unintended activation in some environments, but the capability remains consistent with the stated image-generation purpose.
